details: Bitcoin briefly dropped below $59,000, marking its lowest point since September 2024. This downturn is attributed to broader macroeconomic pressures and a significant sell-off in Asian equity markets. Additionally, spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced substantial net outflows for six consecutive days, with Thursday alone seeing $696.3 million in outflows, the largest since May 27. Ethereum also slid by 3.8% to $1,555.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $59K Amid Macro Pressures and ETF Outflows

details: Ripple has expanded the availability of its USD-pegged stablecoin, RLUSD, into Japan following regulatory approval. This initiative is geared towards institutional liquidity and enterprise payments rather than retail adoption. The move aims to enable Japanese corporations to move dollars across borders instantly using tokenized cash, thereby modernizing cross-border transactions and improving access to working capital for multinational companies.
title: Ripple's RLUSD Stablecoin Expands into Japan for Institutional Payments

details: Morningstar projects that the global stablecoin market could grow to $1.45 trillion by 2035, a significant increase from its current $300 billion. This anticipated growth is driven by promising use cases such as cryptocurrency trading, business-to-business payments, emerging-market deposits, and remittances. While substantial, Morningstar's forecast is more conservative than some industry peers, emphasizing the need for further infrastructure development to achieve widespread adoption.
title: Morningstar Forecasts Stablecoin Market to Reach $1.45 Trillion by 2035

details: The Ethereum Foundation announced a restructuring on June 23, 2026, which involved a 20% reduction in its workforce, affecting 54 employees. This move completes a month-long reorganization linked to a new mandate and treasury management, aimed at making the foundation leaner. The restructuring comes amidst questions regarding the ecosystem's ability to execute through weak market prices and leadership changes.
title: Ethereum Foundation Cuts 20% of Staff Amid Restructuring
